title: Notation
body_md:
We denote by $f\fatsemi g$ the composition of morphisms $f$ and $g$ in diagrammatic order.
	We make generous use of generalized elements, written $x:X$, to talk about objects in categories.
head: manual

label: def:fiber
title: Definition
body_md:
(\textbf{Fiber of a functor})\label{def:fiber}
		Let $P: 
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
 \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$ be a functor. For an object $X  :  
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$, we define the \emph{fiber} of $P$ at $X$ as the subcategory $\mathrm{d} P(X)$ of $
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
$ consisting of those morphisms $\varphi$ in $
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
$ such that $P(\varphi) = \mathrm{id}_X$, which we call \emph{vertical}.

label: def:cart-arr
title: Definition
body_md:
(\textbf{Cartesian arrow})\label{def:cart-arr}
		Let $P: 
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
 \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$. A morphism $\varphi : E \to D$ in $
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
$ is \emph{(strong) $P$-cartesian} if it satisfies the following universal property: let us write $f := P(\varphi)$ and $f : X \to Y$ in $
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$. Then we demand that for any $g : Z \to X$ in $
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$ and any $g' : U \to D$ in $
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
$ with $P(g') = g \fatsemi f$, there exist a unique morphism $h : U \to E$ in $
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
$ with $P(h) = g$ and $h \fatsemi \varphi = g'$:
		\begin{equation}
			\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&, sep=4ex]
				U \\
				Z \& E \& \& D \\
				\& X \& \& Y
				\arrow[dotted, maps to, from=2-2, to=3-2]
				\arrow["{{\exists ! h}}", dashed, from=1-1, to=2-2]
				\arrow[dotted, maps to, from=1-1, to=2-1]
				\arrow["{{\forall g}}"', curve={height=6pt}, from=2-1, to=3-2]
				\arrow["f", from=3-2, to=3-4]
				\arrow["\varphi", from=2-2, to=2-4]
				\arrow[dotted, maps to, from=2-4, to=3-4]
				\arrow["{{\forall g'}}"{description}, curve={height=-24pt}, from=1-1, to=2-4]
			\end{tikzcd}
		\end{equation}

body_md:
(\textbf{Closure properties of fibrations})
		Let $P : 
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
 \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$ be a fibration.
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item If $Q: 
  \relax
  \StrLen{F}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{F}
  \else
    \mathbf{F}
  \fi
 \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
$ is a fibration, then the composite functor $Q \fatsemi P : 
  \relax
  \StrLen{F}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{F}
  \else
    \mathbf{F}
  \fi
 \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$ is a fibration.
			\item If $Q: 
  \relax
  \StrLen{F}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{F}
  \else
    \mathbf{F}
  \fi
 \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$ is any functor, then the pullback
			                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
			\[\begin{tikzcd}[sep=4ex]
			{Q^*
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
} & {
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
} \\
			{
  \relax
  \StrLen{F}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{F}
  \else
    \mathbf{F}
  \fi
} & {
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
}
			\arrow["{Q^*P}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
			\arrow["Q", from=2-1, to=2-2]
			\arrow["P", from=1-2, to=2-2]
			\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
			\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=2-2]
			\end{tikzcd}\]
			is a fibration.
		\end{enumerate}

label: ex:fibs
title: Example
body_md:
(\textbf{Examples of fibrations})\label{ex:fibs}
		For a category $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$, we denote by $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
^\downarrow$ the category of morphisms in $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ with arrows given by the commutative squares.
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item \textbf{Domain fibration}. For any category $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$, the domain projection $\mathrm{dom} := \mathrm{dom}_{
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
} : {
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
}^\downarrow \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ is a fibration. For $u:I \to J$ in $
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$, a cartesian lift of $u$ with respect to an arrow $g : J\to Y$ is given by the square:
			                                                                                                                                                                                                             
			\[\begin{tikzcd}[sep=4ex]
			I & J \\
			X & Y
			\arrow["u\fatsemi g"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
			\arrow[Rightarrow, no head, from=2-1, to=2-2]
			\arrow["u", from=1-1, to=1-2]
			\arrow["g", from=1-2, to=2-2]
			\end{tikzcd}\]
			\item \textbf{Codomain fibration}. If $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ has all pullbacks, then the codomain projection $\mathrm{cod} := \mathrm{cod}_{
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
} : 
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
^\downarrow \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ is a fibration, also called the \emph{fundamental fibration} of $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$. If $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ is locally cartesian closed, the codomain fibration gives rise to a model of \emph{dependent type theory} with $\Sigma$- and $\Pi$-types~\cite{seely1984locally}. The idea is to interpret a type $X$ in context (\emph{i.e.}, a list of free variables) $I$ as a morphism $X \to I$, hence an object of the slice $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
/I$, which is the fiber of $\mathrm{cod}$ at $I :  
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$.

			Given an arrow $u : J \to I$ in $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ together with a map $p : X \to I$, a $\mathrm{cod}$-cartesian lift of $u$ with respect to $p$ is given by pullback:
			\[\begin{tikzcd}[sep=4ex]
			{u^*X} & X \\
			J & I
			\arrow["u", from=2-1, to=2-2]
			\arrow["p", from=1-2, to=2-2]
			\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-1]
			\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
			\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=2-2]
			\end{tikzcd}\]
			This corresponds to substituting the variables in context $I$ along $u$.
			\item \textbf{Simple fibration}. Whereas the codomain fibration models arbitrary dependent types in context $I$, we might want to restrict to the case of \emph{simple types}. A \emph{constant type} is a dependent type over the terminal context $1$, hence a map $X \to 1$, or equivalently, just an object $X$. We can then view $X$ as a type over any context, by considering the pullback:
			\[\begin{tikzcd}[sep=4ex]
			{I \times X} & X \\
			I & 1
			\arrow[from=2-1, to=2-2]
			\arrow[from=1-2, to=2-2]
			\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-1]
			\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
			\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=2-2]
			\end{tikzcd}\]
			Therefore, as soon as $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ admits finite products, the \emph{simple fibration} is given by the subfunctor of $\mathrm{cod}_{
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
}$ spanned by product projections $I \times X \to I$.
			It can also be described, up to fibered equivalence, as follows. Define the category $
  \relax
  \StrLen{S}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{S}
  \else
    \mathbf{S}
  \fi
(
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
)$ by taking as objects pairs $(I,X)$ of $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ and as morphisms $(I,X) \to (J,Y)$ pairs of morphisms $(u : I \to J,f : I \times X \to Y)$ in $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$.
			The simple fibration $S : 
  \relax
  \StrLen{S}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{S}
  \else
    \mathbf{S}
  \fi
(
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
) \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ is the functor defined by $S(I,X) := I$ and $S(u,f) := u$. This is indeed a fibration, where a cartesian lift of $u : I \to J$ with respect to $(J,Y)$ is given by the map $(u,\pi_Y): (I,Y) \to (J,Y)$ with $\pi_Y : I \times Y \to Y$.
			\item \textbf{Subobject fibration}. Let $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ have all pullbacks. We can consider the full subfibration
			\begin{equation}
				\begin{tikzcd}[sep=4ex]
					{{
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
}^\downarrow\vert_\mathsf{mono}} && {
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
^\downarrow} \\
					& {
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
}
					\arrow[hook, from=1-1, to=1-3]
					\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-2]
					\arrow[from=1-3, to=2-2]
				\end{tikzcd}
			\end{equation}
			of monomorphisms in $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$. Quotienting out by the relation that two monomorphisms shall be equal if and only if they factor through each other (necessarily through a monomorphism), we obtain the \emph{subobject fibration} $\mathrm{sub}:{
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
^\subseteq} \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$. The subobject fibration is typically used as an elementary example of fibration of predicates on the objects of $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$.
			\item \textbf{Family fibration}. Consider a category $
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$ with pullbacks and $P : 
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
 \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$ a fibration.

			Let $
  \relax
  \StrLen{Fam}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Fam}
  \else
    \mathbf{Fam}
  \fi
(P) : P \downarrow 
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
 \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$ be the functor constructed as follows:
			\begin{equation}
			\label{eq:fam}
				\begin{tikzcd}[sep=4ex]
					{P\downarrow 
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
} && {
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
} \\
					{
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
^\downarrow} && {
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
} \\
					
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi

					\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-1]
					\arrow["\mathrm{dom}", from=2-1, to=2-3]
					\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-3]
					\arrow["P", from=1-3, to=2-3]
					\arrow["\mathrm{cod}", from=2-1, to=3-1]
					\arrow["{
  \relax
  \StrLen{Fam}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Fam}
  \else
    \mathbf{Fam}
  \fi
(P)}"', curve={height=24pt}, from=1-1, to=3-1]
					\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=2-3]
				\end{tikzcd}
			\end{equation}
			We call $
  \relax
  \StrLen{Fam}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Fam}
  \else
    \mathbf{Fam}
  \fi
(P) : P \downarrow 
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
 \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$ the \emph{family fibration} of $P$. Indeed this is a fibration: any pullback of $P$ is a fibration, so is $\mathrm{dom}^*P$. Since $\mathrm{cod}$ is a fibration, as $
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$ has all pullbacks, then so is their composite $\mathrm{cod} \fatsemi \mathrm{dom}^*P= 
  \relax
  \StrLen{Fam}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Fam}
  \else
    \mathbf{Fam}
  \fi
(P)$. Objects in the fiber $\mathrm{d}
  \relax
  \StrLen{Fam}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Fam}
  \else
    \mathbf{Fam}
  \fi
(P)(I)$ are given by pairs $(f:X \to I, \alpha  :  \mathrm{d} P(X))$. In fact, if $P$ is an arbitrary functor, $
  \relax
  \StrLen{Fam}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Fam}
  \else
    \mathbf{Fam}
  \fi
(P)$ is always an \emph{opfibration}, the \emph{free opfibration} generated by $P$. Thus, $
  \relax
  \StrLen{Fam}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Fam}
  \else
    \mathbf{Fam}
  \fi
(P)$ is both a fibration and an opfibration. One can show that opcartesian transport serves as taking sums (or existential quantification), and that they commute with cartesian transport, serving as reindexing, in a canonical way (via the \emph{Beck--Chevalley isomorphisms}). Hence, the family construction on a fibration $P$ can be understood as the result of freely adding sums to $P$, which are \emph{internally indexed}, \emph{i.e.}, indexed by the base category $
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$. Accordingly, we also write $
  \relax
  \StrLen{Fam}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Fam}
  \else
    \mathbf{Fam}
  \fi
(P)$ for $
  \relax
  \StrLen{Fam}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Fam}
  \else
    \mathbf{Fam}
  \fi
(P)$.

			One could replace $\mathrm{dom}$ in the above definition by a full subfibration of itself, corresponding to a version of the family construction that is the sum completion only with respect to a chosen class of morphisms of $
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$.
		\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
(\textbf{The vertical--cartesian factorization system, {\cite{myers_cartesian_2021}}})
		Let $P: 
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
 \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$ be a fibration.
		The \textbf{vertical--cartesian factorization system} $(\mathrm{vert}, \mathrm{cart})$ induced by $P$ on $
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
$ is an orthogonal factorization system where
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item the left class (\textbf{vertical morphisms}) is given by the maps projecting to isomorphisms and
			\item the right class (\textbf{cartesian morphisms}) is given by cartesian maps.
		\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
Let $P:
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
 \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$ be a fibration. In $
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
$, every cospan:
		\begin{equation}
			                                                                                                                                     
			\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&]
				\& \cdot \\
				\cdot \& \cdot
				\arrow["\mathrm{vert}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
				\arrow["\mathrm{cart}"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
			\end{tikzcd}
		\end{equation}
		admits a pullback:
		\begin{equation}
		\label{eq:carversq}
			                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
			\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&]
				\cdot \& \cdot \\
				\cdot \& \cdot
				\arrow["\mathrm{vert}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
				\arrow["\mathrm{cart}"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
				\arrow["\mathrm{vert}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
				\arrow["\mathrm{cart}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
				\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=2-2]
			\end{tikzcd}
		\end{equation}
		Conversely, every commutative square like~\eqref{eq:carversq} is a pullback square.
head: environment

title: Construction
body_md:
Given a fibration $P : 
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
 \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$, its \textbf{dual} (or \textbf{fiberwise opposite}) is another fibration ${{P}^{\vee_{}}} : {{
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
}^{\vee_{}}} \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$ constructed as follows.

		The category ${{
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
}^{\vee_{}}}$ is the category that has the same objects as $
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
$ and as morphisms equivalence classes of vertical-cartesian spans in $
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
$, i.e.~spans in $
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
$ of the form
		\begin{equation}
			                                                                                                                         
			\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&, sep=small]
				\& {\cdot } \\
				\cdot \&\& \cdot
				\arrow["\mathrm{cart}", from=1-2, to=2-3]
				\arrow["\mathrm{vert}"', from=1-2, to=2-1]
			\end{tikzcd}
		\end{equation}
		They compose because vertical arrows can always be pulled back against cartesian arrows:
		\begin{equation}
			                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
		\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&, sep=small]
			\&\& \cdot \\
			\& {\cdot } \&\&\cdot \\
			X \&\& Y \&\& Z
			\arrow["\mathrm{cart}"{pos=0.8}, from=2-2, to=3-3]
			\arrow["\mathrm{vert}"', from=2-2, to=3-1]
			\arrow["\mathrm{vert}"'{pos=0.3}, from=2-4, to=3-3]
			\arrow["\mathrm{cart}", from=2-4, to=3-5]
			\arrow["\mathrm{vert}"', from=1-3, to=2-2]
			\arrow["\mathrm{cart}", from=1-3, to=2-4]
			\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125, rotate=-45}, draw=none, from=1-3, to=3-3]
		\end{tikzcd}
		\end{equation}
		Hence this defines a category, and $P$ still works as a projection onto $
  \relax
  \StrLen{X}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{X}
  \else
    \mathbf{X}
  \fi
$.

		The fibration structure comes from noticing one can still lift arrows to cartesian arrows. More easily, since our fibrations are cloven, we can define
		\begin{equation}
			{{P}^{\vee_{}}} := \intop (\mathrm{d} P \fatsemi (-)^\mathsf{op})
		\end{equation}
		which is a fibration by construction.
		This point of view will be also useful later on.

title: Definition
body_md:
(\textbf{Action of a monoidal category})
	\label{def:actegories}
		Let $(
  \relax
  \StrLen{M}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{M}
  \else
    \mathbf{M}
  \fi
, I, \otimes)$ be a monoidal category.
		A \emph{(left) $
  \relax
  \StrLen{M}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{M}
  \else
    \mathbf{M}
  \fi
$-action on the category $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$} is a functor $\bullet : 
  \relax
  \StrLen{M}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{M}
  \else
    \mathbf{M}
  \fi
 \times 
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
 \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ together with coherent isomorphisms witnessing $I \bullet A \cong A$ and $M \bullet (N \bullet A) \cong (M \otimes N) \bullet A$.
		The action is \emph{strict} when such isomorphisms are in fact identities.

label: def:preoptics
title: Definition
body_md:
(\textbf{Preoptic})
	\label{def:preoptics}
		Fix a strict monoidal category $
  \relax
  \StrLen{M}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{M}
  \else
    \mathbf{M}
  \fi
$ and two strict left $
  \relax
  \StrLen{M}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{M}
  \else
    \mathbf{M}
  \fi
$-actions $(
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
,\bullet)$ and $(
  \relax
  \StrLen{D}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{D}
  \else
    \mathbf{D}
  \fi
, \circ)$.
		Let $A,S : 
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ and $B,T  :  
  \relax
  \StrLen{D}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{D}
  \else
    \mathbf{D}
  \fi
$ be objects.
		A \emph{preoptic} $
  \relax\if@display
	 
	 \begin{pmatrix}{\vphantom{f_f^f}B} \\ {\vphantom{f_f^f}A} \end{pmatrix}

  \else
	 
	 \begin{psmallmatrix}{\vphantom{f}B} \\ {\vphantom{f}A} \end{psmallmatrix}

  \fi
 \leftrightarrows 
  \relax\if@display
	 
	 \begin{pmatrix}{\vphantom{f_f^f}T} \\ {\vphantom{f_f^f}S} \end{pmatrix}

  \else
	 
	 \begin{psmallmatrix}{\vphantom{f}T} \\ {\vphantom{f}S} \end{psmallmatrix}

  \fi
$ is a triple $(M,f,f^\sharp)$ where $M  : 
  \relax
  \StrLen{M}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{M}
  \else
    \mathbf{M}
  \fi
$ is called the \emph{residual}, $f:A \to M \bullet S$ is a morphism in $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ called the \emph{view}, and $f^\sharp : M \circ T \to B$ is a morphism in $
  \relax
  \StrLen{D}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{D}
  \else
    \mathbf{D}
  \fi
$ called the \emph{update}.
		The category of \emph{preoptics} $
  \relax
  \StrLen{PreOptic}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{PreOptic}
  \else
    \mathbf{PreOptic}
  \fi
_{\bullet,\circ}$ has objects pairs of an object of $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ and an object of $
  \relax
  \StrLen{D}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{D}
  \else
    \mathbf{D}
  \fi
$, and morphisms preoptics.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Using preoptics instead of optics is a convenient device to avoid working with \emph{2-optics} instead, in which the quotient hinted at above is replaced by explicit witnesses.
		Avoiding the quotient, however, seems necessary for the fibrational manipulation of optics, see e.g.~\cite{braithwaite_fibre_2021}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Something stronger is true: $Q$ is actually a \emph{fibration of fibrations}, i.e.~a `fiberwise fibration', since B\'enabou showed that fibrations in $
  \relax
  \StrLen{Fib}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Fib}
  \else
    \mathbf{Fib}
  \fi
(
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
)$ are given by maps of fibrations \emph{which are themselves fibrations}.
		A published account of this fact can be found in~\cite{hermida_properties_1999}.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $(L, R)$ be a factorization system on $
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
$. An \textbf{ambifibration} $A : 
  \relax
  \StrLen{P}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{P}
  \else
    \mathbf{P}
  \fi
 \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
$ is a functor such that
		\begin{enumerate}
			\item every arrow in $L$ has an opcartesian lift ($A$ restrics to an opfibration on $L$)
			\item every arrow in $R$ has a cartesian lift ($A$ restrics to a fibration on $R$)
		\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Definition
head: environment

title: Example
body_md:
If $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ is a cartesian monoidal category, then the total category of its associated simple fibration $S:
  \relax
  \StrLen{S}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{S}
  \else
    \mathbf{S}
  \fi
(
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
) \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ is again cartesian, meaning we can form towers of arbitrary height by iterating the construction of simple fibrations.
head: environment

title: Example
body_md:
Likewise, when $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ is finitely complete we can form towers $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
^{\downarrow^n} \to \cdots \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
^\downarrow \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ of arbitrary height where the $i$-th level is the category of \emph{$i$-dimensional commutative cubes} in $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$.
head: environment

title: Example
body_md:
More generally, suppose $P:
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
 \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ is a \emph{full comprehension category}~\cite{jacobs_comprehension_1993}, meaning it admits a right adjoint $1:
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
 \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
$ (a \emph{fibered terminal object}) as well as a further right adjoint (\emph{comprehension}) $\{-\}:
  \relax
  \StrLen{E}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{E}
  \else
    \mathbf{E}
  \fi
 \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$.
		By repeatedly pulling back $P$ along $\{-\}$ we can form towers of fibrations of arbitrary height.

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $\boldsymbol{P}$ be a tower of fibrations of length $n$.
		The morphisms in the total space of its iterated dual ${{\boldsymbol{P}}^{\vee_{n}}}$ are called \textbf{$\boldsymbol{P}$-dialenses}.
head: environment

title: Example
body_md:
As anticipated, optics can be constructed as dialenses of height $2$, if of a bizarre kind.
		First, recall from~\cite{braithwaite_fibre_2021} that every (strict, for simplicity) action $\bullet : 
  \relax
  \StrLen{M}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{M}
  \else
    \mathbf{M}
  \fi
 \times 
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
 \to 
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ of a monoidal category $
  \relax
  \StrLen{M}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{M}
  \else
    \mathbf{M}
  \fi
$ on a category $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ can be repackaged as a 2-opfibration $
  \relax
  \StrLen{Para}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Para}
  \else
    \mathbf{Para}
  \fi
(\bullet) \to B
  \relax
  \StrLen{M}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{M}
  \else
    \mathbf{M}
  \fi
$, where $
  \relax
  \StrLen{Para}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Para}
  \else
    \mathbf{Para}
  \fi
(\bullet)$ is the bicategory of $
  \relax
  \StrLen{M}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{M}
  \else
    \mathbf{M}
  \fi
$-parametric $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$-morphisms (see~\cite{Capucci_2022}) and the projection to $B
  \relax
  \StrLen{M}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{M}
  \else
    \mathbf{M}
  \fi
$ is given by projection out the parameter of a morphism.
		Here let's ignore the 2-dimensional information and just consider this as an opfibration (because every 2-opfibration has an underlying 1-opfibration, cf.~\cite[Definition~2.1]{hermida_properties_1999}).

		Recall the 1-dimensional data of $
  \relax
  \StrLen{Para}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Para}
  \else
    \mathbf{Para}
  \fi
(\bullet)$: its objects are the same of $
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
$ while its 1-cells are pairs $(m \in 
  \relax
  \StrLen{M}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{M}
  \else
    \mathbf{M}
  \fi
, f:m \bullet X \to X)$, composing in the obvious way.

		Opcartesian lifts for the functor $
  \relax
  \StrLen{Para}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Para}
  \else
    \mathbf{Para}
  \fi
(\bullet) \to B
  \relax
  \StrLen{M}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{M}
  \else
    \mathbf{M}
  \fi
$ are constructed as follows:
		\begin{equation}
			                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
			\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&]
				{
  \relax
  \StrLen{Para}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Para}
  \else
    \mathbf{Para}
  \fi
(\bullet)} \& X \& {m \bullet X} \\
				{B
  \relax
  \StrLen{M}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{M}
  \else
    \mathbf{M}
  \fi
} \& \ast \& \ast
				\arrow["P_\bullet"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
				\arrow["m"', from=2-2, to=2-3]
				\arrow["{(m, 1_{m \bullet X})}", from=1-2, to=1-3]
			\end{tikzcd}
		\end{equation}
		Further on, we'll abbreviate $(m, 1_{m \bullet X})$ with $m_X$.

		Then given two left $
  \relax
  \StrLen{M}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{M}
  \else
    \mathbf{M}
  \fi
$-actegories $(
  \relax
  \StrLen{C}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{C}
  \else
    \mathbf{C}
  \fi
,\bullet)$ and $(
  \relax
  \StrLen{D}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{D}
  \else
    \mathbf{D}
  \fi
, \circ)$, one can construct the following tower of opfibrations:
		\begin{equation}
			                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
			\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&, sep=5ex]
				{
  \relax
  \StrLen{Para}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Para}
  \else
    \mathbf{Para}
  \fi
(\circ) \times_{B 
  \relax
  \StrLen{M}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{M}
  \else
    \mathbf{M}
  \fi
} 
  \relax
  \StrLen{Para}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Para}
  \else
    \mathbf{Para}
  \fi
(\bullet)} \& {
  \relax
  \StrLen{Para}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Para}
  \else
    \mathbf{Para}
  \fi
(\circ)} \\
				{
  \relax
  \StrLen{Para}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Para}
  \else
    \mathbf{Para}
  \fi
(\bullet)} \& {B 
  \relax
  \StrLen{M}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{M}
  \else
    \mathbf{M}
  \fi
} \\
				{B
  \relax
  \StrLen{M}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{M}
  \else
    \mathbf{M}
  \fi
}
				\arrow["{P_\circ}", from=1-2, to=2-2]
				\arrow["{P_\bullet}", from=2-1, to=2-2]
				\arrow["{P_\bullet}"', from=2-1, to=3-1]
				\arrow[from=1-1, to=1-2]
				\arrow["{P_\circ}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
				\arrow["\lrcorner"{anchor=center, pos=0.125}, draw=none, from=1-1, to=2-2]
			\end{tikzcd}
		\end{equation}
		Then its iterated dual produces preoptics (Def.~\ref{def:preoptics}):
		\begin{equation}
			                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
			\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&]
				{ 
  \relax
  \StrLen{PreOptic}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{PreOptic}
  \else
    \mathbf{PreOptic}
  \fi
_{
  \relax
  \StrLen{M}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{M}
  \else
    \mathbf{M}
  \fi
}(\bullet, \circ)} \& U \& \textcolor{red}{m \circ U} \& \textcolor{red}{V} \& V \\
				{{{
  \relax
  \StrLen{Para}[\catarglen]
  \ifnum\catarglen=1
    \mathcal{Para}
